name: radio-table
title: Radio table
description: Compare while you choose: a radio per row, the specs in columns, a real table to a screen reader and cards on a phone.
docs: columns describe the table: the first column is the name of each choice and carries the radio, the others are the figures to compare, each with an optional align (start, center or end, the default), format (how the value is written) and speak (how it is read out). rows give a value, their cells by column key, an optional note under the name, and disabled: true, or a string that says why. To a screen reader it is a table with headers, and every radio is described by its row read in column order ("8 GB memory, 4 CPUs, 160 GB disk, 48 euros per month"); underneath the radios are real radio inputs that share one name, so there is one tab stop and the arrow keys move and choose. Where the container is narrower than 560px each row is a card with the heading beside each figure. name and required work as on any radio group in a form, and locale writes the numbers of columns without a format.
